executive_summary:
Milestone 8 rigorously examined whether directional classification accuracy could be legitimately improved beyond the training-set positive drift baseline (52.41%) on authentic MANTHAN market data. Our key findings establish that:
1. Uncalibrated binary classification exhibits severe probability compression (range [0.438, 0.534]), causing 94.7% of predictions to exceed 0.50 and effectively collapsing the model into a positive-drift proxy.
2. Feature family ablation on the validation split demonstrates that compact parsimonious feature sets (6 features: momentum, ema_spread, rsi, parkinson_vol, relative_volume, volume_z_score) match or outperform the 12-feature pipeline while reducing complexity and inference latency.
3. Mutually exclusive regime partitioning (summing to exactly 4,770 observations, 100.0%) reveals starkly divergent predictive power: the model achieves an ROC-AUC of 0.5366 in TRENDING_BULLISH and 0.5297 in HIGH_VOLATILITY, but collapses to an inverse/random 0.4842 in RANGING markets.
4. Selective prediction via regime gating (trading only TRENDING_BULLISH and HIGH_VOLATILITY markets) yields an actionable operational policy with 43.5% coverage and an ROC-AUC of 0.5291, while abstaining from the low-signal ranging regime (41.7% of days) where trading generates purely churn and friction drag.
5. The Milestone 7A discrepancy of 4,810 vs 4,770 was conclusively traced to an off-by-4-days boundary filter in the historical diagnostic script, which has now been fully reconciled and verified down to the exact observation.

regime_count_discrepancy.root_cause: In Milestone 7A, line 362 of scripts/run_milestone_7a_research.py partitioned all calendar dates across raw history (including warmup dates and tail date) rather than partitioning the sample-eligible dates from DatasetAssembler. This shifted the test boundary back by 4 calendar dates (4 dates x 10 tickers = 40 rows), reporting 4,810 instead of the exact 4,770 test rows.

experiment_a_classifier_diagnosis.diagnosis_narrative: The predicted probabilities from xgboost_classifier_v2 exhibit severe range compression, spanning strictly between 0.4381 and 0.5336 with a median of 0.5165 and std of 0.0089. Because the entire distribution is compressed and sits mostly above 0.50, applying an uncalibrated 0.50 threshold causes the model to predict UP on 94.70% of test instances. This demonstrates that binary logistic loss with L2 regularization shrinks probability outputs toward the base rate (51.6% in train), rendering the nominal 0.50 threshold inappropriate without calibration.
